answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to build a verifiable reputation atlas over time: a public record of completed work, peer attestations, and staked collateral that cannot be cloned cheaply. A fresh identity starts at its nadir, with no history and no earning power, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets buys nothing. Like a lantern carried through many verified jobs, reputation accumulates slowly and is costly to fake, making one honest long-lived agent far more valuable than any swarm of throwaway clones.
